prerequisites: Fluency with Differential and Integral Calculus content taught in high school is recommended.

learning_outcomes.text: Recognize and understand the basic methodologies of linear algebra; geometry; differential geometry; differential and integral calculus; differential and partial differential equations; numerical methods; numerical algorithms; statistics, and optimization that are applied to engineering.
Solve, using mathematics and statistics, potential problems that may arise in engineering.
Propose creative solutions to satisfactorily respond to real needs and problems of society.
Develop professional texts and scientific-technical reports according to the conventions of the industrial technical engineering field.
Adapt the organization of content and the use of language, verbal and non-verbal, to argue in various situations or before various audiences.
Show the advantages and opportunities of different solutions to the same problem in a critical and constructive way.
Apply the principles and methods of quality.

syllabus_topics: Block I: SEQUENCES AND SERIES OF REAL NUMBERS
TOPIC 1.- SEQUENCES OF REAL NUMBERS
Cardinality of a set. Countable sets.
Sequence of real numbers. Limit of a sequence. Calculation of limits.
Convergence criteria for a sequence of real numbers.
TOPIC 2.- SERIES OF REAL NUMBERS
Definition and properties of a series of real numbers.
Convergence and sum of a series.
Series of positive real numbers: Convergence criteria.
Sum of some types of series.
Alternating series. Series with positive and negative terms.
Block II: LIMITS AND CONTINUITY OF FUNCTIONS OF ONE AND SEVERAL VARIABLES
TOPIC 1.- LIMIT AND CONTINUITY OF A REAL FUNCTION OF A REAL VARIABLE.
Limit of a function at a point.
Infinitesimals and infinities.
Equivalent functions.
Continuity of a function at a point.
Types of discontinuities.
Properties of continuous functions.
TOPIC 2.- LIMIT AND CONTINUITY OF FUNCTIONS OF SEVERAL REAL VARIABLES.
Real function of n real variables.
Real function of two variables: Domain, range, graph.
Limit of a function of two variables.
Continuity of functions of two variables.
Block III: DIFFERENTIAL CALCULUS OF FUNCTIONS OF ONE AND SEVERAL VARIABLES.
TOPIC 1.- DERIVABILITY IN FUNCTIONS OF ONE VARIABLE
Derivative of a function at a point: Geometric interpretation.
Calculation of derivatives.
Continuity of differentiable functions.
Derivative of the inverse function and of the composite function.
Successive derivatives. Implicit differentiation.
Differential of a function.
Properties of differentiable functions.
Relative extrema: Existence conditions and calculation. Absolute extrema.
Concavity. Convexity. Inflection points.
TOPIC 2.- DERIVATIVES OF FUNCTIONS OF SEVERAL REAL VARIABLES.
Partial derivative of a function of n variables.
Partial derivatives in functions of two variables: Geometric interpretation.
Successive partial derivatives.
Formula for finite increments for functions of two variables.
Directional derivative, gradient vector and differentiability of a function of two variables.
Relative extrema in functions of two variables: Existence conditions and calculation.
Divergence and curl.
Block IV: INTEGRAL CALCULUS OF FUNCTIONS OF ONE AND SEVERAL VARIABLES.
TOPIC 1.- DEFINITE INTEGRAL
Definite integral. Geometric interpretation.
Fundamental Theorem of Calculus. Barrow's Rule.
Properties of the definite integral.
Calculation of primitives.
Improper integrals.

Applications of the definite integral: Calculation of plane areas. Length of a planar curve arc. Volume of a body by homothetic sections. Volume of a body of revolution. Area of a surface of revolution.
TOPIC 2.- MULTIPLE INTEGRALS
Double integral.
Change of variable in the double integral.
Applications of the double integral.
Triple integral.
Change of variable in the triple integral.
Applications of the triple integral.
teaching_methods: Problem/exercise solving in the ordinary classroom
assessment_rules: Two practical case tests will be conducted in the classroom, primarily practical but also evaluating theoretical and operational knowledge. Continuous assessment values the submission of solutions to problems proposed during the course development.
